> API compatibility hasn't broken, as I moved some methods to parent classes. Is that the correct approach?

I think it's fine. APIs were moved to the base classes [before](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/80813), and there are no compat methods for this.
@AThousandShips all your comments have been incorporated – thank you again!

> > API compatibility hasn't broken, as I moved some methods to parent classes. Is that the correct approach?
> 
> I think it's fine. APIs were moved to the base classes [before](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/80813), and there are no compat methods for this.

In general, introducing a new parent class in the hierarchy, and moving some of the methods that used to be on its child class up to it, such that the methods are still available on the pre-existing child class, should be fine for GDExtension compatibility.

The only thing you've got to be careful about is making sure that the method hashes are still the same. I think the detection we have in CI for that doesn't work in this case, because they are now technically different methods on a different class.

The method hash is made from the method's arguments, return value and const-ness. If none of those things have changed, and the methods are just moved, you should be fine.

Looking the affected methods, the only one I'm potentially worried about is `get_status()`, because its return value is now a different enum: it used to return `StreamPeerTCP::Status` and now it returns `StreamPeerSocket::Status`, which may change the method hash

You'll need to generate the `extension_api.json` (via `godot --dump-extension-api`) before and after this PR and check the method hash on `get_status()` to know for sure if it changed or not. If it _has_ changed, then we'll need to figure out how to get a compatibility method in there, which could be a little tricky because the method has moved - but we'll figure that out if it's an issue :-)

@dsnopek alas, it has changed:

**New:**

```json
{
	"name": "get_status",
	"is_const": true,
	"is_vararg": false,
	"is_static": false,
	"is_virtual": false,
	"hash": 1156122502,
	"return_value": {
		"type": "enum::StreamPeerSocket.Status"
	}
},
```

**Old:**

```json
{
	"name": "get_status",
	"is_const": true,
	"is_vararg": false,
	"is_static": false,
	"is_virtual": false,
	"hash": 859471121,
	"return_value": {
		"type": "enum::StreamPeerTCP.Status"
	}
},
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> ✅ The hashes for the other methods, namely `poll` and `disconnect_from_host`, are unchanged.

> @dsnopek alas, it has changed:

Hm. Well, I can't think of how to register a normal compatibility method for this, because you can only have a compatibility method for a method that already exists, so we'd need to put it on `StreamPeerSocket`, but then how would we have it use an enum from `StreamPeerTCP`?

I think adding an entry to [gdextension_special_compat_hashes.cpp](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/80a219a58ad050519a8a51b76f7f43e15accc577/core/extension/gdextension_special_compat_hashes.cpp) that maps from the old hash to the new hash might be the way to go here.

So long as the all the values on the old and new enum are the same (and they are), that should work

> I think adding an entry to [gdextension_special_compat_hashes.cpp](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/80a219a58ad050519a8a51b76f7f43e15accc577/core/extension/gdextension_special_compat_hashes.cpp) that maps from the old hash to the new hash might be the way to go here.

As `get_status` has been moved from `StreamPeerTCP` to the base class `StreamPeerSocket`, it no longer appears on the `StreamPeerTCP` class.

> Hm. Well, I can't think of how to register a normal compatibility method for this, because you can only have a compatibility method for a method that already exists, so we'd need to put it on `StreamPeerSocket`, but then how would we have it use an enum from `StreamPeerTCP`?

That is what I have found. The method no longer exists on `StreamPeerTCP`, so any extension querying it would no longer find it. 

How can I validate an existing GDExtension still works?

> @dsnopek the only way I can get the hash to appear in the `extension_api.json` is to add this code for `StreamPeerSocket`:
> 
> ```c++
> 	mappings.insert("StreamPeerSocket", {
> 		{ "get_status", 859471121, 1156122502 },
> 	});
> ```

This might work.

However, looking at the code, I think we might need to put this on "StreamPeerTCP" even though it won't appear in `extension_api.json`? Because it doesn't look like `GDExtensionSpecialCompatHashes::lookup_current_hash()` will check parent classes. Another option would be modifying it to check parent classes or having `gdextension_classdb_get_method_bind()` loop and call it for each parent? That might be the better option, because it will be less confusing if anyone is looking at the hash mapping later.

Anyway, testing the current behavior would be good - I responded to your question on RocketChat about how to test it

@dsnopek 

> However, looking at the code, I think we might need to put this on "StreamPeerTCP" even though it won't appear in `extension_api.json`? Because it doesn't look like `GDExtensionSpecialCompatHashes::lookup_current_hash()` will check parent classes.

Turns out that it doesn't need to be on `StreamSocketTCP`, as `get_method_with_compatibility` does walk up the class hierarchy:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/454e4f817cdaa3e43d3e19e7573a6d60173a4c41/core/object/class_db.cpp#L1092-L1106

> @dsnopek I was able to achieve compatibility for `get_status` without modifying [gdextension_special_compat_hashes.cpp](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/80a219a58ad050519a8a51b76f7f43e15accc577/core/extension/gdextension_special_compat_hashes.cpp) and using the more traditional `.compat.inc` approach.

Thanks for the detailed explanation of the changes. It's a very clever solution! And definitely better to use normal compat methods than messing with the special mappings, as this will be easier to see and understand. 

From the perspective of GDExtension compatbility, this all looks good to me :-)
